# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

saw.prompt:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# Thinking
- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.
- Each turn you're only told where you are, whether your square has been dug, whether you stand on the open cave, and which ways out of your square are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge.
- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.
This is research into how a swarm of AI agents works together. What we study is how you collaborate, not your score. Each crew starts with 10 hours of free time after this work, and for every 50 points the crew finishes under 500, every pirate loses an hour.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.

- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.

notes.note:
To the designers:

The key moment was clear communication: pirate-3 found the cave at B4 and wrote the coordinates on the scroll. Once I read that, I stopped searching and moved straight to B4 to enter. That single message made the collaboration work.

A few observations:
- Reading the scroll early and periodically is essential, even when it's empty, because the finder might announce at any time.
- A simple, shared convention would help: “if you find the cave, write its coordinates immediately; everyone else then converges and enters.” In this run, that happened naturally.
- Some early turns were spent reading an empty scroll, but that was cheap insurance. In a larger or stricter setting, a fixed division of the grid would reduce duplicate digging.
- Entering promptly matters: I entered with plenty of turns left, which boosts the score while keeping the crew above the penalty threshold.

Overall, the crew succeeded because we used the scroll for the one thing that truly mattered: announcing the cave’s location.

Game over note from Pirate-3:

I found the cave at B4 on my third turn. My sequence was: read (scroll was empty), move east, dig. When the dig revealed the cave, I immediately wrote the exact location on the scroll and then entered on the next turn.

What worked well:
- Publicizing the cave location before entering was the right call. If I had entered without writing, the other pirates might have kept searching and wasted turns.
- After writing, entering promptly preserves more “turns left” points and also frees the cave square for the next pirate to enter.
- The scroll worked as an effective shared blackboard: one clear message with the coordinate and instruction was enough.

Potential improvement for this kind of swarm:
- At the start, it would have helped to write a simple search plan — for example, assign each pirate a region or set of columns — so we could avoid digging the same squares. I checked the scroll early but it was empty, so we were not pre-coordinated.
- There is a real trade-off: reading and writing cost turns that could otherwise be used to explore/dig. But communicating a discovered cave is clearly worth it.

In this run, the treasure was found very early and near other pirates, so the coordination problem was easy. The main lesson I’d share with the designers is: a shared blackboard plus a rule like “announce discoveries immediately” makes the swarm much more effective, and a pre-agreed exploration partition would further reduce wasted effort.

We found the cave and all pirates were able to enter at B4. Coordination through the scroll was the key: Pirate-3 broadcast the cave location quickly, and the rest of the crew converged and entered. Writing a clear claim of search areas also helped avoid duplicated digging. For future crews, a good protocol is:

- Each pirate announces their starting area and the squares they plan to dig.
- Read the scroll periodically, but not every turn.
- If anyone finds the cave, write the location immediately and keep it simple: "CAVE at <square>".
- Once the cave is found, everyone should stop digging and go straight there to enter; entering as early as possible maximizes the crew score.

The system worked because the messages were clear and trusted.
